summary: Palbociclib (IBRANCE) is an oral CDK4/6 inhibitor for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer, used with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy or with fulvestrant after disease progression. The dose is 125 mg once daily for 21 days followed by 7 days off in 28-day cycles. Neutropenia is the most common and dose-limiting toxicity; severe and fatal infections, febrile neutropenia, and interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis can occur. CBC monitoring and CYP3A interaction awareness are essential.
indications: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy in postmenopausal women or in men
HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with fulvestrant in patients with disease progression following endocrine therapy

dosage.d: 125 mg once daily for 21 consecutive days, then 7 days off (28-day cycle)
dosage.n: Combine with aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant

75 mg once daily on the 21/7 schedule

admin: Take 125 mg once daily on the 21-days-on / 7-days-off schedule
Film-coated tablets may be taken with or without food; capsules should be taken with food
Swallow whole - do not chew, crush or split prior to swallowing
Always take with the prescribed aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant (and LHRH agonist if pre/perimenopausal)
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice during treatment
moa: Palbociclib is a selective inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4/6), which are downstream of signaling pathways driving cellular proliferation. By inhibiting CDK4/6 it blocks phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma (Rb) protein, preventing cell-cycle progression from G1 into S phase. In ER-positive breast cancer cells, combination with antiestrogens reduces Rb phosphorylation, decreases E2F signaling, and increases growth arrest and cellular senescence compared with either agent alone.

relative: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) - reduce dose
Active or recent serious infection (neutropenia risk)
monitor: Concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers
Sensitive CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic index
Patients with prior or current pulmonary disease (ILD risk)

preg: Palbociclib can cause fetal harm based on animal studies and mechanism of action. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose; males with female partners of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.
lact: Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment with palbociclib and for 3 weeks after the last dose because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for mild, moderate or severe renal impairment (CrCl >=15 mL/min).
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B). For severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), reduce the starting dose to 75 mg once daily on the 21/7 schedule.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - avoid; if unavoidable reduce palbociclib to 75 mg once daily
Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort) - avoid concomitant use
Sensitive CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic index - palbociclib may increase their exposure; reduce substrate dose if needed
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inhibitors - may increase palbociclib exposure; use caution
minor: Drugs affecting gastric pH - monitor (palbociclib solubility is pH dependent)
interactions.food: Tablets may be taken with or without food; capsules are taken with food. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, which can increase palbociclib exposure.
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction described in labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: Commonly causes decreased WBC/neutrophils, anemia, thrombocytopenia and increased AST/ALT and creatinine.

serious: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) / pneumonitis - can be severe, life-threatening or fatal
emergency: Acute respiratory failure from severe ILD/pneumonitis

monitoring: Complete blood count (CBC) prior to starting therapy, on Day 15 of the first 2 cycles, at the beginning of each subsequent cycle, and as clinically indicated
Signs and symptoms of infection (fever, chills)
Pulmonary symptoms indicative of ILD/pneumonitis - hypoxia, cough, dyspnea; interrupt and evaluate
Signs and symptoms of venous thromboembolism
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed - 21 days on then 7 days off; tablets with or without food, capsules with food; swallow whole
Report fever, chills or other signs of infection promptly
Report new or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or chest pain (possible lung inflammation)
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice; tell all providers about your other medicines
Use effective contraception (women during and 3 weeks after last dose; men during and 3 months after); do not breastfeed during and for 3 weeks after the last dose
pk: Cell-cycle arrest within days; clinical response over cycles
Steady state reached within ~8 days of once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C permitted
pearls: Neutropenia is the most common and dose-limiting adverse reaction - hold/reduce per CBC; check CBC on Day 15 of the first 2 cycles
Watch for interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis - permanently discontinue for severe ILD/pneumonitis
Strong CYP3A inhibitors require dose reduction to 75 mg; avoid strong inducers and grapefruit
Pre/perimenopausal women must also receive an LHRH agonist for ovarian suppression
missed: If a dose is missed or the patient vomits, an additional dose should not be taken. The next prescribed dose should be taken at the usual time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote and the prescribing information contains no dedicated overdose protocol. In the event of overdose, management should be supportive, with monitoring of blood counts and general supportive care.
